label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
**One star for now: promising software, unacceptable migration and support**

Bridger Bend Community Library is a one-branch library with two full-time staff members, volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year, $14,200-per-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud in June 2026 and went live October 19.

Since October 28, we have been able to check out materials only offline, on one laptop. Our holds queue was wiped, and approximately 640 holds are gone. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to pick up his held large-print Westerns. We had no record of his hold and had to send him home with nothing. One of our volunteers is now writing checkouts on index cards, like it’s 1975.

Our support ticket has been open for 12 days. We have received three replies, each saying the issue has been “escalated to engineering.” That is not an adequate response for the system our community depends on every day.

To be fair, Stackhouse Cloud looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is honestly better than our old system. The problem is not the product idea. It is the migration and support we have received. Our sales representative promised “a dedicated migration specialist.” What we got was a shared inbox.

I am asking for a named person in Stackhouse’s leadership to call me this week, take ownership of this situation, and provide a concrete plan for restoring service and addressing the lost holds. Small libraries do not have spare staff, spare laptops, or spare patience for weeks of unexplained downtime.

My advice to other directors, especially at small libraries: before signing, get support response times in writing. Ask who will be responsible for your migration, how escalations work, and what happens when something goes wrong after go-live. A good demo is not a support plan.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and this line item is on the agenda. I would like to be able to tell our commissioners that Stackhouse has responded and resolved these problems. Right now, I cannot.

I will revisit this review if Stackhouse fixes the problems and provides the support we were promised. Until then, this remains a one-star review.
